newsitem.title: UK: UK local authority funds up cash amid market fears.
newsitem.headline: UK local authority funds up cash amid market fears.

text.p: British local authority pension funds built their cash holdings to historic highs in the first quarter amid expectations of a correction in major markets.

Performance measurement constancy WM Company said on Thursday an annual survey of 100 local authority pension funds with total assets of about 65 billion sterling showed cash holdings at 8.6 percent at the end of March -- the highest since the analysis began 15 years ago.
UK pension funds as a whole held 6.1 percent in cash at the same time.
WM Company said local authority funds posted total returns of 11.1 percent in the year to end March -- slightly ahead of all UK pension funds which returned 11 percent.

UK equities, representing about half of total assets, was the top performing sector in the year with average returns of 17.6 percent. But the sector fell short of the 18.7 percent return in the FTSE All-Share Index.

"A large proportion of the underperformance came in the first quarter of 1997 and a key reason was the relatively low weighting compared to the index in the pharmaceutical and finance sectors," said WM director Peter Warrington.
Overseas equities, representing some 20 percent of assets, returned a disappointing 1.4 percent. It said funds suffered after pulling some money out of North America.
Holdings in North America have fallen below three percent of assets, which Warrington said was surprising given that the area represents around half of the world's stockmarket capitalisation.
"Some funds have no North American exposure at all and have clearly been expecting a major correction."
Average annual returns over the past ten years in the local authority funds stand at 10.9 percent and over five years 14.9 percent.
